title: James Clear's '2-Minute Gateway' For Hard Habits
alt_title_1: Twyla Tharp's 5:30 AM Taxi Cab Trick for Unbreakable Consistency
alt_title_2: Why You Should Stop Habits After 120 Seconds on Day 1
description_hook: Choreographer Twyla Tharp and 'Atomic Habits' author James Clear share one rule for hard habits: shrink any ambitious goal down to a 120-second gateway ritual until showing up becomes automatic.

scenes.headline: Never Start a 60-Minute Habit on Day One
scenes.stat_label: MAXIMUM TIME ALLOWED TO TRIGGER A NEW HABIT
bullets: Big 1-hour plans collapse on your first tired Tuesday
You cannot optimize a routine you fail to start
scenes.narration: Never try to launch a sixty-minute habit from scratch. Master the first one hundred twenty seconds instead, because you cannot optimize a habit you never start.
scenes.source: James Clear, Atomic Habits (2018), the Two-Minute Rule

scenes.headline: Twyla Tharp's 5:30 AM Taxi Cab Ritual
scenes.stat_label: HAILING THE CAB WAS THE ACTUAL HABIT
bullets: She worked out for two hours each morning
Her ritual: get dressed and hail a New York cab
scenes.narration: In Atomic Habits, James Clear shares choreographer Twyla Tharp's morning ritual. She wakes at five-thirty, puts on her workout clothes, and hails a cab to the gym. The ritual is not the workout. It is getting in the cab.
scenes.source: Twyla Tharp, The Creative Habit (2003); James Clear, Atomic Habits (2018)

scenes.headline: Turn Heavy Goals Into Frictionless Gateways
scenes.left_body: Write 2,000 words tonight / Study coding for 90 minutes
scenes.right_body: Open the blank doc + type 1 sentence / Run 1 line of code
scenes.narration: Once the taxi door closed, momentum took over. Apply the same physics to your work: replace write two thousand words with open the document and type one ugly sentence.

scenes.headline: Standardize Before You Optimize
scenes.stat_label: 5 DAYS X 2 MINS BEATS 0 DAYS X 2 HOURS
scenes.stat_subtext: Starting burns 10x more mental fuel than continuing in motion
scenes.narration: Starting is the hardest part. Make showing up your standard first, then add more once the habit sticks.

scenes.headline: Win the First 2 Minutes Tonight
scenes.stat_label: SHRINK YOUR NEXT GOAL TO 120 SECONDS
bullets: Make the entry step too small to skip on bad days
Identity builds from streaks, never one heroic burst
